notes: Shooter: a first-person round-based game with scoring, respawns, sniper zoom and AI bots. A crossroads of four long streets meeting at one junction is lane-network — routes that channel traffic into a predictable engagement front — and the author's answer that the road ends are a long sniper range apart confirms the sight lines down each arm, with the junction itself as the choke-bottleneck. The only enemies the prompt actually describes are the AI noobs that spawn when the server is empty, so PvE Shooter is the closest preset and spawner-npc is a stated feature rather than an addition; I dropped its building-interior because nothing goes indoors and it would add an unready P3, and added cover-los as the street furniture that gives a small modern city crossroads its cover without closing the long lanes. With no user to ask, I treated the press-play lobby as a small staging room that neither the prompt nor the author's answers describe spatially, so it does not drive the shape or force a separate-map route, and read the 3-second spawn force field, the random respawn points, the 5-minute round and the on-screen score as mechanics with no geometry to build.
